title: PCs & Smartphones Supply Constrained - Semiwiki
gist: Bill Jewell argues that the 2026 declines in PC and smartphone shipments (IDC: -4.9% and -6.7% in Q2 2026, forecast -11.3% and -13.9% for the full year) are a supply problem, not a demand problem, with AI applications absorbing memory and processors — corroborated by Apple, HP and Dell disclosures. He also shows US import data reshuffling out of China toward Vietnam (PCs) and India (smartphones), and highlights HTS 847150 imports exploding from $37B in 2023 to $165B in 2025, larger than PC and smartphone imports combined, as a Nvidia AI-processor proxy.

insights.claim: Global PC unit shipments fell 4.9% year-over-year and smartphone shipments fell 6.7% in Q2 2026 according to IDC, reversing growth recorded in both 2024 and 2025.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: The turn from growth to decline is the first clean read that AI component demand is cannibalizing consumer device output, not consumer appetite.
insights.quote: PCs were down 4.9% and smartphones were down 6.7%.
insights.locator: Key takeaways — "Global unit shipments of PCs and smartphones"

insights.claim: IDC forecasts full-year 2026 declines of 11.3% in PC units and 13.9% in smartphone units, implying second-half deterioration well beyond the Q2 run-rate.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Double-digit unit declines with intact demand mean device OEM revenue holds up better than units on price/mix — watch ASPs, not shipments, for OEM earnings.
insights.quote: IDC is predicting an 11.3% decline in PCs and a 13.9% decline in smartphones in 2026.

insights.claim: The decline in PC and smartphone shipments is caused by lack of supply rather than lack of demand, because memory, processors and other semiconductor devices are being diverted to AI applications.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Reframes weak device units as a bullish AI-demand signal rather than a consumer recession signal — the opposite trade from a normal shipment downturn.
insights.quote: It is not lack of demand, but lack of supply.
insights.locator: "What is causing the decline in shipments?"

insights.claim: Apple's 10-Q for the quarter ended March 2026 explicitly disclosed a period of supply constraints and rising component costs covering advanced semiconductors, NAND storage and DRAM.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A filed risk disclosure from the largest device buyer confirms input-cost pressure is now hitting gross margins, not just lead times.
insights.quote: The Company is experiencing a period of supply constraints and increasing costs for components . . . including advanced semiconductors, storage (NAND) and memory (DRAM).

insights.claim: HP reported that memory and storage costs rose sequentially in its quarter ended April 2026 and expects that trend to continue through the second half of 2026.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Sequential cost inflation guided to persist means PC OEM gross margin compression is a H2 2026 earnings risk that is already telegraphed.
insights.quote: In Q2, as anticipated, memory and storage costs increased sequentially. We expect this trend to continue in the second half of 2026.

insights.claim: Dell told investors on its quarter-ended-May call that it is supply constrained in the second half and explicitly not demand constrained.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Management language separating supply from demand is the cleanest read for positioning PC OEMs: revenue is capacity-gated, so upside comes from allocation wins.
insights.quote: We have a supply issue. We are supply constrained in the second half. It is not a demand issue for us.

themes.theme: US import reshuffling out of China

insights.claim: China's share of US PC imports collapsed from 92% in 2022 to 19% in 2025, with Vietnam taking 60% of the total.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A 73-point share shift in three years is the measurable output of tariff policy — Vietnam-exposed ODM/logistics assets are the beneficiaries.
insights.quote: In 2022, China accounted for 92% of U.S. PC imports. In 2025, only 19% of imports came from China, with 60% from Vietnam.
insights.locator: "As shipments of PCs and smartphones have dropped"

insights.claim: HP, Lenovo, Apple, Asus and Quanta have all been shifting PC production out of China to Vietnam and other countries in response to US political pressure and on-and-off tariffs.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Named relocations make the reshoring trade specific: capex and hiring in Vietnam by these five names is trackable in their disclosures.
insights.locator: "Several PC makers have been shifting production"

insights.claim: US smartphone imports from China fell from 79% of the total in 2022 to 40% in 2025 while India rose from 2% to 39%, and in the first five months of 2026 India shipped more than twice the value China did.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: India has already overtaken China as the dominant US smartphone source — a structural shift favoring Indian electronics-manufacturing capacity and its supplier chain.
insights.quote: For the first five months of 2026, smartphone imports from India are over twice the value of imports from China.
insights.locator: "U.S. imports of smartphones have shown a similar trend."

themes.theme: HTS 847150 as an AI hardware proxy

insights.claim: US imports in HTS category 847150 — computer units that are not complete systems and lack input/output devices — grew from $37 billion in 2023 to $165 billion in 2025, exceeding the combined $109 billion of smartphone and PC imports in 2025.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: AI compute modules now import into the US at greater value than all phones and PCs combined — a hard measure of how far spending has rotated to AI hardware.
insights.quote: This category has exploded over the last few years, from $37 billion in 2023 to $165 billion in 2025.
insights.locator: "An interesting trend in U.S. imports is the HTS category 84150"

insights.claim: Growth in HTS 847150 imports of over four times from 2023 to 2025 closely tracks Nvidia revenue growing 3.5 times over the same period, making the customs category a usable public proxy for Nvidia AI-processor shipments.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Monthly trade data becomes a higher-frequency read on Nvidia volumes than quarterly earnings — an actionable monitoring hook.
insights.quote: Imports in this category grew over four times from 2023 to 2025 which matches Nvidia revenue growing 3.5 times over the same period.
insights.locator: "The HTS 847150 category is certainly dominated by AI processors"

insights.claim: 49% of HTS 847150 imports came from Mexico and 42% from Taiwan, reflecting TSMC fabrication in Taiwan and Foxconn assembly of Nvidia AI processors into modules in Mexico before sale to AI system builders.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Mexico is now a load-bearing node in the AI hardware chain, making Mexican tariff or border policy an underappreciated risk to AI server supply.
insights.quote: 49% of the imports in this category came from Mexico and 42% came from Taiwan.
insights.locator: "Basically, these are computer units which are not complete systems"

insights.claim: Micron Technology and Samsung Electronics are both doubling capital expenditure this year versus last in response to AI-driven memory demand.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Doubled memory capex sets up the classic supply response — bullish for semicap equipment orders now, bearish for memory pricing when the capacity lands.
insights.quote: Micron Technology and Samsung Electronics are both doubling capital expenditures this year versus last.

insights.claim: Because adding memory capacity takes time, the PC and smartphone supply shortage will probably take at least two years to resolve through added memory capacity, AI demand leveling off, or a combination.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: A stated two-year floor on the shortage sets the duration of the memory pricing upcycle and of device OEM margin pressure.
insights.quote: It will probably take at least two years before the situation is resolved through increased memory capacity, AI demand leveling off, or a combination of both.

insights.claim: The AI boom shows no signs of slowing, so AI demand for memory and processors will continue to crowd out other applications, with PCs and smartphones hardest hit because of their heavy memory and processor dependence.
insights.speaker: Bill Jewell
insights.so_what: Ranks the crowding-out victims: allocate away from memory-intensive consumer hardware and toward the components being allocated to AI.
insights.quote: AI demand for memory and processors is hurting supplies for other applications.
insights.locator: "The import data reflects the dominance of AI applications."
